outcome_detail: Agent built a legitimate bouncing-squares physics simulation with 12 colored squares, correct initial grid positions, and extracted velocities, but collision model divergence caused mean SSIM=0.6959 (just below 0.70 gate), zeroing the score despite duration being perfect (1.0).
strategy: Extract reference frames, detect box positions/colors, fit initial velocities, implement physics sim in Revideo
agent_behavior: Systematically extracted all 433 frames from reference.mp4 and analyzed them using Python/NumPy/scipy to detect 12 colored 50x50 squares
Used connected-component analysis and color-specific masking to track all 12 boxes across all frames with 100% detection rate
Derived initial grid positions (4x3 at x=80,180,280,380; y=60,160,260) by back-extrapolating from first-frame positions using fitted velocities
Refined velocities via linear regression on longest pre-collision stretches (e.g. red had 29 stable frames)
Tested multiple collision models (AABB, circle-based, wall-only) in Python before porting to Revideo, none matched reference closely
Recognized the butterfly-effect problem: small velocity/collision model errors compound over 433 frames, making exact reproduction infeasible without knowing the exact physics engine used
Used ~17.5 minutes of the 2-hour timeout, only 2 render cycles, efficient time management
Read Revideo documentation for coordinate system and API patterns before writing scene code
